column4: Visit note | 2025-05-14 10:00 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Farzana Hasan, 23, female. Ms. Hasan reports experiencing nausea along with the pain and painful cramps in the first days of each period. She mentions these symptoms have become worse since taking a job with long standing hours in Kamrangirchar, where she works as a cricket coach. She has a history of Bronchial asthma. On examination, her pain score is 7/10, BP is 122/75 mmHg, pulse is 72 bpm, and weight is 78 kg. Heart and lung sounds are clear. Assessment: Primary dysmenorrhoea. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to use a hot water bottle, do light exercise, and keep a period diary. Follow-up in 3 months with the period diary.

Visit note | 2025-05-17 04:00 PM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Obaidul Kabir, 38, male. Mr. Kabir comes in reporting itchy dry patches on the elbows and knees and scratching at night, which flared during the dry winter in Mohammadpur. He works as a construction worker. He has no known comorbidities. On examination, the affected area is about 9 cm across, BP is 111/85 mmHg, pulse is 86 bpm, and weight is 85 kg. The skin shows dry, erythematous plaques over the extensor surfaces. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: referral to Endocrinology in this clinic for further assessment; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up after the Endocrinology review.

Visit note | 2025-05-18 03:00 PM | Dr. Sabrina Chowdhury, Cardiology | Patient: Nabila Karim, 58, female. Mrs. Karim states she has no other complaints apart from occasional dizziness and headaches on waking. She notes this was first picked up at a pharmacy in Rajshahi while buying other medicines. She works as a ride-share driver and has a history of Hypothyroidism. On examination, her BP is 178/98 mmHg, pulse is 91 bpm, and weight is 85 kg. Heart sounds are normal without murmurs. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-05-20 02:00 PM | Dr. Faisal Karim, Psychiatry | Patient: Jewel Sheikh, 38, male. Mr. Sheikh complains of poor sleep, tense muscles, and feeling restless, which began after witnessing a road accident in Jatrabari. He works as a journalist and has no other major medical conditions. On examination, his GAD-7 score is 11, BP is 129/85 mmHg, pulse is 77 bpm, and weight is 66 kg. He appears anxious but oriented in time and place. Assessment: Generalized anxiety disorder. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to practise slow breathing daily, reduce tea and coffee, and start counselling sessions. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-05-21 03:30 PM | Dr. Rafiqul Islam, Cardiology | Patient: Kamal Islam, 71, male. Mr. Islam reports having no symptoms, high cholesterol on a routine test, and a father who had a heart attack at 55. He works as a tailor and noted the finding was from an office health check in Mohammadpur. He has no reported comorbidities. On examination, his LDL cholesterol is 5.7 mmol/L, BP is 135/79 mmHg, pulse is 90 bpm, and weight is 77 kg. Cardiovascular examination is unremarkable. Assessment: Dyslipidaemia. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to reduce fried food, red meat, and ghee, walk 30 minutes daily, and aim to lose 3 kg. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat lipid profile.

Visit note | 2025-05-24 12:00 PM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Marium Alam, 29, female. Ms. Alam presents with acne and irregular periods, which she noticed after a friend in Keraniganj suggested testing. She works as an accountant and has no other chronic illnesses. On examination, her BMI is 28.9, BP is 129/72 mmHg, pulse is 77 bpm, and weight is 93 kg. Examination shows mild hirsutism and normal systemic findings. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-05-24 12:30 PM | Dr. Mostafizur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Bilkis Haque, 57, female. Mrs. Haque complains of stiffness in the morning for a few minutes and knee pain on the stairs, which is worse since standing all day at a shop in Faridpur. She works as a rickshaw puller and has no other significant medical history. On examination, her BMI is 27.9, BP is 134/74 mmHg, pulse is 82 bpm, and weight is 58 kg. Range of motion in both knees is slightly limited with mild crepitus. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. She was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-05-25 04:00 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Dipak Ghosh, 51, male. Mr. Ghosh reports symptoms worse in winter, itchy dry patches on the elbows and knees, and scratching at night, which flared during the dry winter in Cumilla. He works as a nurse and has no known comorbidity. On examination, the affected area is about 10 cm across, BP is 131/83 mmHg, pulse is 77 bpm, and weight is 65 kg. Skin inspection reveals dry scaly plaques on bilateral elbows and knees. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only; no new medicine was prescribed today. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.
